message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Update static assets

on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '.github/workflows/update.yml'
  workflow_dispatch: {} # Used to manually trigger a nightly build.
  schedule:
    # Run on 1st and 15th of each month
    - cron: '1 2 1,15 * *'

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  NODE_VERSION: '22'

jobs:
  update:
    name: Update static assets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Checkout source
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          ref: develop
      - name: Enable Yarn 4.x
        run: corepack enable
      - name: Setup NodeJS ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: 'yarn'
      # The scripts require some modules that we need to install.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: yarn install --immutable
      - name: Config git
        run: |
          git config --local user.email "action@github.com"
          git config --local user.name "GitHub Action"
      # Update CSL files
      - name: Update CSL files
        run: |
          yarn update:csl
          git add -A
          git diff-index --quiet HEAD || git commit -m "chore(citeproc): Update CSL files"
      # Update the CITATION.cff file if applicable
      - name: Update CITATION.cff
        run: |
          yarn update:citation
          git add -A
          git diff-index --quiet HEAD || git commit -m "Update CITATION.cff"
      # Test to make sure we don't break anything
      - name: Test build
        run: yarn test
      - name: Push changes
        uses: ad-m/github-push-action@v1.0.0
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          branch: develop",
  "rationale": "The update job has no explicit timeout, so a runaway or hung step can consume unbounded runner time. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by measured evidence on a comparable CI workflow (26.82% elapsed savings) and literature-reported VM-time reductions (12.9% free, 8.1% paid). Historical runs for this workflow complete in roughly 28-39 seconds, so a 5-minute timeout provides ample headroom for valid slow runs while bounding runaway consumption. The change is minimal (one job-level key), preserves every existing step, the test build, the push, permissions, and all triggers, and adds no privileged actions, secrets, or network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
